cards.front: Recall a key point about Culture & Communication
cards.back: Individualist cultures (e.g. USA, UK) prioritise personal goals, independence and individual rights. Collectivist cultures (e.g. Japan, China) prioritise group harmony, interdependence and social obligations. These values affect communication styles, conformity and self-concept.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Culture & Communication
cards.back: High-context cultures (e.g. Japan, Arab nations) rely heavily on NVC, context and shared understanding - much is left unsaid. Low-context cultures (e.g. Germany, USA) rely on explicit, direct verbal communication - meaning is in the words.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Culture & Communication
cards.back: Cultural differences in conformity: collectivist cultures show higher conformity rates (Smith & Bond's meta-analysis). This reflects different values - conformity is seen positively as maintaining group harmony in collectivist cultures, but negatively as weakness in individualist cultures.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Culture & Communication
cards.back: Culture and self-concept: independent self-construal (individualist - self is separate from others) vs interdependent self-construal (collectivist - self is defined through relationships). Markus & Kitayama showed these different self-views affect cognition, emotion and motivation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Culture & Communication
cards.back: Ethnocentrism: judging other cultures by the standards of your own. Much early psychological research was conducted in Western, Educated, Industrialised, Rich, Democratic (WEIRD) societies and may not generalise to other cultures. Henrich et al. (2010) showed WEIRD participants are not representative of humanity.

cards.front: What should you know about psychology exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating cross-cultural research, always consider: is the comparison fair? Are measures culturally appropriate? Are researchers being ethnocentric? Have findings been replicated across diverse cultures?

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: People from collectivist cultures are always more conformist and less individualistic than people from individualist cultures. Correct: While collectivist cultures show higher conformity on average, there is huge variation within cultures. cards.front: Key Studies and Theories in Culture & Communication
cards.back: Culture & Communication is a core topic in GCSE Psychology that requires understanding of key studies, theories and research methods. The AQA, OCR and Edexcel specifications all require you to know specific studies in detail, evaluate their methodology, and apply psychological concepts to real-life scenarios. cards.front: Applying Culture & Communication to Real Life
cards.back: GCSE Psychology requires you to apply psychological understanding of culture & communication to everyday situations. Consider how the theories and studies you have learned about explain real behaviour: How does culture & communication affect people in schools, workplaces, families and communities?
